question: What is the SI unit of acceleration?
solution:
The correct answer is __**m s⁻²**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The SI unit of acceleration is the meter per second squared (m/s²).
 
• Acceleration is defined as the rate of change of velocity with respect to time.
 
• In the SI system, it is derived from the base units of length (meter) and time (second).
 
• This unit is universally used in physics and engineering to quantify acceleration.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Velocity and Speed**

 
 
• Velocity is a vector quantity that refers to the rate at which an object changes its position.
 
• Speed is a scalar quantity that refers to how fast an object is moving regardless of direction.
 
 
 
• **Newton's Second Law of Motion**
 
 
• States that the acceleration of an object is directly proportional to the net force acting on it and inversely proportional to its mass (F=ma).
 
• This law is fundamental in understanding the relationship between force, mass, and acceleration.
 
 
 
• **Uniform and Non-uniform Acceleration**
 
 
• Uniform acceleration occurs when the velocity of an object changes by an equal amount in every equal time period.
 
• Non-uniform acceleration occurs when the velocity changes by unequal amounts in equal time periods.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Acceleration**
 
 
• Acceleration is a key concept in various fields such as automotive engineering, aerospace, and biomechanics.
 
• Understanding acceleration is crucial for designing safety systems in vehicles and optimizing performance in sports.
